sourcedFrom: Staccato XC Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato (Published August 26, 2024)
cleanIntro: A 2011 strip out of Staccato's own XC instructions: slide stop, slide forward off the frame, then the Dawson Precision tool-less guide rod captured on its takedown lever and rotated clear of the link. The comp is part of routine cleaning on this one, not an afterthought.

steps.title: Gun clear, workspace clear of ammunition
steps.action: Before anything moves, confirm the pistol is clear and get the loose ammunition off the bench. Staccato asks for the workspace itself, not just the gun — a round left on the mat is how a stripped pistol gets reloaded by accident on reassembly.
steps.quote: Ensure your gun is clear, and your workspace is free of ammunition.
steps.cite: Staccato XC Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 1

steps.title: Racked, and checked in both chamber and magwell
steps.action: Pointed somewhere safe, rack the slide to the rear and look into the chamber and the magazine well — both. On a 2011 the ejection port hides a case rim from one angle depending how you hold it, which is why the check is two places and not one.
steps.quote: With the pistol pointed in a safe direction, rack the slide to the rear and visually inspect the chamber and magazine well make sure the pistol is empty.
steps.cite: Staccato XC Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 2

steps.title: Notch aligned, slide stop pushed through and removed
steps.action: Draw the slide back until the takedown notch lines up with the knuckle of the slide stop, hold it there, and push the slide stop pin through from the opposite side with a finger or a small tool. It should move under light pressure — if it fights you, the notch has drifted off the knuckle.
steps.quote: Pull the slide back to line up the take down notch on the slide with the slide stop knuckle push the slide stop pin from the opposite side of the pistol using a finger or a small tool and remove the slide stop.
steps.cite: Staccato XC Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 3

steps.title: Slide eased forward off the frame
steps.action: Run the top end gently forward off the frame rails and set the frame down. Keep it level — tipping it lets the recoil assembly start to move inside the slide before it has been captured.
steps.quote: Gently pull the slide forward off of the frame.
steps.cite: Staccato XC Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 4

steps.title: Flange pushed forward to expose the tool-less rod's takedown lever
steps.action: Push forward on the flange of the guide rod. That compresses the spring far enough to bring the takedown lever on the Dawson Precision tool-less rod into reach. No bushing wrench and no plug wrestle — the tool-less rod is the whole reason this strip differs from a conventional 1911.
steps.quote: Remove the Dawson Precision® Tool-Less Guide Rod, by pushing forward on the flange of the guide rod to expose the take-down lever.
steps.cite: Staccato XC Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 5

steps.title: Lever lowered onto the reverse plug ledge to capture the system
steps.action: Depress the lever and lower it onto the front ledge of the reverse plug. That captures the recoil system as one unit so the spring cannot get away from you. Keep hold of the flange until you feel the lever settle onto the ledge.
steps.caution: The spring is compressed and held only by that lever on the ledge. An uncaptured tool-less rod under load will launch — do not let the flange slip forward while you are seating the lever.
steps.quote: Depress the lever and lower it down onto the front ledge of the reverse plug to capture the system.
steps.cite: Staccato XC Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 6

steps.title: Recoil system out of the spring tunnel, rotated clear of the link
steps.action: Take the captured assembly out from the shooter's side of the spring tunnel, turning it slightly as it comes so it clears the barrel link. This is where the XC's published procedure differs from the P's — it comes out of the tunnel with a rotation, not straight out the back.
steps.quote: Remove recoil system from the shooter side of the spring tunnel, rotating it slightly to clear the link.
steps.cite: Staccato XC Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 7

steps.title: Link forward, barrel out of the muzzle end
steps.action: Flip the link forward along the barrel so it clears, then draw the barrel out of the muzzle end of the slide. That completes the strip — frame, slide, captured recoil assembly and barrel. Staccato publishes nothing further than this.
steps.quote: Slide the link forward on the barrel and pull it out from the muzzle end of the slide.
steps.cite: Staccato XC Disassembly — step-by-step disassembly and reassembly instructions — Featured article, Maintenance Monday series, by Staccato — Disassembly, step 8

deepAbsentReason: Staccato publishes this page as basic disassembly and reassembly — the article describes itself as covering 'basic disassembly/reassembly of the Staccato XC', and it ends at barrel, slide, frame and the captured recoil assembly. No extractor, firing pin, sear, mainspring housing or grip-module procedure is published on it, and no exploded view accompanies it. For anything beyond what is written, the page directs owners to contact Staccato Customer Service directly. Nothing deeper was invented from it.

cleaning.name: RAILS, FRAME & FEED RAMP
tasks: Brush and wipe debris off the slide rails and the frame surfaces
Clear the barrel feed ramp — carbon here is what starts feeding trouble
Wipe the breech face and under the extractor claw

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Brush the bore from breech to muzzle using the memory flex cable, repeating as needed
Put a small amount of CLP on a bore mop and oil the bore
Wipe the excess back out with a clean patch — a film, not a wet bore

cleaning.name: COMPENSATOR
tasks: Take the carbon out of the inside of the comp with a brush or a scraper
Apply a thin layer of CLP to the inside of the comp
Check the comp is still tight before it goes back into service

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: A few drops of lubricant on the slide rails
A few drops on the barrel contact points
Wipe the captured recoil assembly and check the spring for kinks before reassembly

reassembly: Check the link is flipped forward toward the muzzle, then reinstall the barrel.
Rotate the guide rod into place and push on the rear of the flange to release the takedown lever, then lower it gently into place.

Line the slide rails up with the frame rails and run the slide on. Staccato's own note: the flange must be pushed up against the barrel and not kicking out toward the frame, and the barrel must be rotated correctly so it will seat inside the frame.

Look through the slide stop hole in the frame for the link — the slide stop's pin must pass through the link's hole or the pistol will not function. If it is not lined up, drop it into place with a small tool.
Insert the slide stop through the link hole and rest it gently against the frame.
Pull the slide back to line the takedown notch up with the slide stop knuckle, then seat the slide stop fully.
Rack the slide to check for proper function.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty, rack the slide and confirm it returns fully into battery, check the slide stop is seated flush and locks the slide back on an empty magazine, and confirm the thumb and grip safeties both function before handling.
